name: Outflow Valve Travel Limiter
rem: (O)(M) May be inoperative provided: a) The Outflow Valve Travel Limiter is verified inoperative in retracted position, and b) Flights are conducted at or below FL 250.
oproc: Flights are conducted at or below FL 250.
mproc: For an inoperative Outflow Valve (OFV) Travel Limiter, confirm that the travel limiter of the OFV is inoperative in the retracted position as follows: 1. On the PRESSURIZATION control panel, push the AUTO PRESS switch. 2. On the EICAS display, confirm that (STATUS) message CABIN PRESS MAN is displayed. 3. On the PRESSURIZATION control panel, lift the switch guard and push the EMER DEPRESS switch. 4. On the EICAS display, confirm that (CAUTION) message EMER DEPRESS ON is displayed. 5. Through the valve (or the muffler if installed), visually confirm that the OFV is fully open. NOTE: Valve butterfly must be at 90° position inside the valve body to be considered fully open. 6. On the PRESSURIZATION control panel, lift the switch guard and push the EMER DEPRESS switch. 7. On the EICAS display, confirm that (CAUTION) message EMER DEPRESS ON is NOT shown. 8. On the PRESSURIZATION control panel, push the AUTO PRESS switch. 9. On the EICAS display, confirm that (STATUS) message CABIN PRESS MAN is NOT shown.
ploc: On PRESSURIZATION Control Panel
ptext: Outflow Valve Travel Limiter INOP

name: Bus Power Control Unit (BPCU) Protective Functions Degradation
rem: (O) One or both may be degraded.
oproc: For a degraded BPCU Protective Function: 1. If INFO message 24 ELECTRICAL FAULT − BPCU 1 DEGRADED is displayed, dispatch the aircraft. No further action is required. OR 2. If INFO message 24 ELECTRICAL FAULT − BPCU 2 DEGRADED is displayed, it is possible that APU start cannot be accomplished using aircraft batteries. a. Attempt APU start using aircraft batteries. 1) If successful, this means that the 24 ELECTRICAL FAULT − BPCU 2 DEGRADED message was not caused by a BATT2 HES power supply fault. Dispatch the aircraft. No further action is required. 2) If not successful, this means that the 24 ELECTRICAL FAULT − BPCU 2 DEGRADED message was caused by a BATT2 HES power supply fault and external power will be required to start the APU on ground. APU is considered inoperative for dispatch and deferred per 49-00-03A, however, APU operation on ground using external power is permitted. OR 3. If both 24 ELECTRICAL FAULT − BPCU 1 DEGRADED and 24 ELECTRICAL FAULT − BPCU 2 DEGRADED info messages are displayed, it is possible that APU start cannot be accomplished using aircraft batteries. a. Attempt APU start using aircraft batteries. 1) If successful, this means that the 24 ELECTRICAL FAULT − BPCU 2 DEGRADED message was not caused by a BATT2 HES power supply fault. Dispatch the aircraft. No further action is required. 2) If not successful, this means that the 24 ELECTRICAL FAULT − BPCU 2 DEGRADED message was caused by a BATT2 HES power supply fault and external power will be required to start the APU on ground. APU is considered inoperative for dispatch and deferred per 49-00-03A, however, APU operation on ground using external power is permitted.
ploc: Below Landing Gear Control
ptext: Panel BPCU Protection Function DEGRADED

oproc: 1. Select BATT 2 to AUTO. 2. On the ELEC synoptic page make sure DC ESS 1, DC ESS 2 and DC ESS 3 are powered by BATT 2. 3. Make sure BATT 2 voltage reads no less than 25 V DC. 4. Make sure BATT 1 voltage reads no less than 25 V DC. 11. Select EXT PWR to “IN USE”. 12. Confirm the following messages are not displayed: - BATT 1 FAIL (Caution) - - CONTINUED NEXT PAGE

name: Emergency Exit
rem: May be inoperative provided associated overwing emergency exit slide pressure is verified to be operative PRIOR TO EACH DEPARTURE, (Logbook Entry Required). Repetitive Check Required (Yellow Placard)
mproc: PRIOR TO EACH DEPARTURE, (Logbook Entry Required): For an inoperative Overwing Emergency Exit Slide Condition Indication, before each flight, select one of the methods that follow to make sure that the pressure indicator needle of the exit slide is within the green band: 1. Method 1. a. Do the extension of the flaps and the slats to Position 5 (full extend) (refer to BD500−A−J27−53−00−01AAA−913A−A). b. Get access to the Aft Flap Track Panel (195BL(196BR)) Box Seal − Overwing Wing to Body Fairing (WTBF). c. Use a mirror and a flashlight to make sure that the pressure indicator needle, of the OWEED escape slide, is in the green band. d. Do the retraction of the flaps and the slats to position 0 (refer to BD500−A−J27−53−00−02AAA−913A−A). OR 2. Method 2. a. Put a WARNING placard on the OWEED escape slide to prevent all operation. b. Disconnect the OWEED escape slide short cable (refer to BD500−J−52−21−17−01AAA−510A−A). c. Rotate the OWEED escape slide and make sure that the pressure indicator needle, of the OWEED escape slide, is in the green band. d. Connect the OWEED escape slide short cable (refer to BD500−J−52−21−17−01AAA−730A−A). e. Remove the WARNING placard from the OWEED escape slide.
ploc: Below The Landing Gear Control Panel.
ptext: OWEE SLIDE CONDITION IND INOP

For an inoperative or missing Refuel/Defuel Adapter Cap, once each flight day, make sure there is no evidence of fuel leaking from the Refuel/Defuel Adaptor as follows: 1. (680.39 kg) of fuel in each fuel wing tank, and make sure there is enough space in the center tank to allow fuel transfer. 2. The remaining sidestick procedure (b. 2) have to be executed as per AFM/FCOM2. 2. Do the following check: a. Make sure left engine is not running. b. On the HYDRAULIC panel turn the 2B switch to ON. c. On the HYDRAULIC panel turn the PTU switch to ON. d. Confirm the following messages are not displayed: - HYD 1 LO PRESS (Caution) - 29 HYDRAULIC FAULT − HYD PTU PRESS SW INOP (Info) e. On the HYDRAULIC panel turn the PTU switch to OFF. f. On the HYDRAULIC panel turn the 2B switch to OFF. g. Start the left engine. h. rem: be inoperative provided: a) Manual mode is operative, and b) Alternate procedures are used.
oproc: 31-21-01B For an inoperative automatic update function of the clock indications on the Adaptive Flight Display (AFD), set the time manually as follows: 1. On the Control Tuning Panel (CTP), turn the BRT/OFF knob to the OFF position. 2. Wait a few seconds and turn the BRT/OFF knob toward the BRT position. NOTE: This is done to reset the CTP and unlock access to the MANUAL TIME function. 3.On the CTP, press the TUNE/MENU button once. 4. Press the CLOCK Line Select Key (LSK), to bring up the CLOCK page. 5. If MANUAL TIME is displayed, press the upper left LSK. 6. Rotate the outer ring of the TUNE/DATA knob to move the focus indicator. 7. Rotate the inner knob to increase or decrease the time and date values. 8. When done, press the upper left LSK to save the new time setting.

name: Landing Gear Actuation System, Alternate Extension System
rem: (O)(M) May be inoperative provided: a) There is no evidence of external leakage of hydraulic fluid, b) Nose and main landing gear are secured in down position for dispatch, c) Landing gear control valve is deactivated, d) No revenue passengers are carried, e) Flight is prohibited in known or forecasted icing conditions, f) Performance penalties are applied, and g) Repairs are made within 1 flight day.
oproc: 1. Flight is prohibited in known or forecasted icing conditions. 2. Refer to ODM Reference FLIGHT WITH LANDING GEAR DOWN. 3. Apply the following Performance Corrections. 32-30-00 LANDING GEAR ACTUATION SYSTEM, ALTERNATE EXTENSION SYSTEM EFFECTIVITY All FLIGHT PLANNING 1. When Automated Flight Plan System is used, use Performance Code LGD (if REQUIREMENTS available), or 2. When Automated Flight Plan System is NOT available, use conservative factors in ODM to compute the flight planning data. NOTES Make a notation on the Flight Plan when Enroute Climb is limiting. AWABS Performance corrections have been applied. TAKEOFF Manual WDR not permitted with MEL 32-30-00. PERFORMANCE WORKSHEET
mproc: For an inoperative landing gear actuation system/alternate extension system: 1. Lock the landing gear assemblies in the DOWN position (refer to BD500−A−J10−10−01−01AAA−720A−A and BD500−A−J10−10−01−02AAA−720A−A). 2. Deactivate the Landing Gear Control Valve (LGCV) (refer to BD500−A−J32−31−12−01AAA−560A−A. NOTE: For dispatch purpose, make sure to remove all “REMOVE BEFORE FLIGHT” safety flags from the locking pins.

ptext: Panel LANDING GEAR ACTUATION ALTERNATE EXTENSION SYSTEM INOP

name: Brake Temperature Monitoring System (BTMS)
rem: (O)(M) May be inoperative provided ODM procedures are performed.
oproc: For an inoperative BTMS, refer to ODM – Abnormal – Brake Cooling section for minimum brake cooling times following landing or a rejected takeoff.” NOTE: At crew change, inbound crew should leave details of landing weight and Vapp used for next crew to calculate brake cooling times. If no data forwarded, next operating crew should assume maximum landing weight for their calculations.
mproc: For an inoperative BTMS, do a general visual inspection of the visible components of the brakes. 1. Confirm there is no visible damage. 2. Confirm the Brake Temperature Sensors (BTS) and the Electric Motor Actuators (EMAs) are safely secured. 3. Check the brake wear condition on each of the wear pins. NOTE: Fully worn condition is shown when the wear pin is flush with the brake carrier plate.

mproc: Do a check of the nose and main tire pressures ONCE EACH FLIGHT DAY, (Logbook Entry Required): 1. For the nose tire pressure, fill with nitrogen as required refer to BD500−A−J12−10−32−01AAA−214A−A. 2. For the main tire pressure, fill with nitrogen as required refer to BD500−A−J12−10−32−02AAA−214A−A.

NOTE 1: Any portion of the system that operates normally may be used. NOTE 2: For the waste tank ultrasonic point level sensor (100%), refer to item 38−32−03.
mproc: For an inoperative generic component of the lavatory waste system: 1. Deactivate or isolate associated components. 2. Ensure that the associated components are not leaking. If both waste tank ultrasonic level sensors are deactivated the whole lavatory waste system will become inoperative. 3. Make sure that the following Onboard Maintenance System (OMS) fault messages are displayed: - LAVATORY/WATER SYSTEM FAULT - 75% ULTRASONIC POINT LEVEL SENSOR (MT78) NO CAN BUS DATA TRANSMISSION / REPORTED BY WWSC - CONTINUED NEXT PAGE

name: Throttle Quadrant Assembly (TQA) – Thrust Reverser Balk Function
placard: TQA THRUST REVERSER BALK FUNCTION INOP
rem: may be inoperative provided operations are not dependent on its use. NOTE: Maximum reverse thrust is available by extra pilot effort (at a nominal force of 25 lbs.).
oproc: 1. For an inoperative left Thrust Reverser Balk Function, as indicated by the INFO message 76 L ENGINE FAULT − THROTTLE REV BALK INOP, ensure the INFO message 76 R ENGINE FAULT − THROTTLE REV BALK INOP is NOT displayed. OR 2. For an inoperative right Thrust Reverser Balk Function, as indicated by the INFO message 76 R ENGINE FAULT − THROTTLE REV BALK INOP, ensure the INFO message 76 L ENGINE FAULT − THROTTLE REV BALK INOP is NOT displayed. 3. If the Balk Function fails while engaged, the max available reverse thrust will be idle reverse. a. Dispatch landing limits are not calculated with any reverse thrust credit. b. Inflight assessment of landing distance with reduced reverse thrust may be obtained from the ODM or an ACARS LPR request. 4. If the Balk Function fails to engage: a. positively verify when selecting reverse thrust that the thrust reverser is fully deployed at idle (green “REV” indicated on the EICAS N1 gauge) prior to increasing reverse thrust RPM. b. positively verify that the thrust reverser is fully stowed at idle (white “REV” indication extinguished on the EICAS N1 gauge) prior to increasing forward thrust RPM.
ploc: On the Throttle Quadrant Assembly
ptext: TQA THRUST REVERSER BALK FUNCTION INOP

name: Thrust Reverser System
rem: (O)(M) One may be inoperative provided: a) Inoperative thrust reverser is stowed and locked, and b) Performance penalties are applied.
oproc: 1. Operations on runways contaminated with ice are prohibited. 2. Move only the throttle lever associated with the operative Thrust Reverser (TR) to reverse thrust range when the TR is used during landing. 3. The maximum crosswind component for takeoff and landing on a wet runway is limited to 25 knots. NOTE: When the Thrust Reverser is stowed and locked, the associated L(R) REVERSER INHIBIT (status) and L(R) ENGINE FAULT (advisory) messages may be displayed and the related Thrust Reverser INFO message will go out of view. 4. Apply the following Performance Corrections. 78-30-02 THRUST REVERSER SYSTEM EFFECTIVITY All FLIGHT PLANNING Operations on runways contaminated with ice are prohibited. REQUIREMENTS NOTES The limiting crosswinds for takeoff and landing on a WET runway is 25 kts. AWABS Performance corrections have been applied. TAKEOFF Manual WDR not permitted with MEL 78-30-02. PERFORMANCE WORKSHEET
mproc: For an inoperative thrust reverser, deactivate the inoperative thrust reverser (refer to BD500-A-J78-30-00- 01AAA-181A-A). NOTE: When the Thrust Reverser Isolation Control Unit (ICU) inhibit lever is pushed to the lock out position, the associated L(R) REVERSER INHIBIT (Status) message will be displayed and the related thrust reverser info message will go out of view.
ploc: On the Throttle Quadrant Assembly
ptext: THRUST REVERSER SYSTEM REDUNDANCY INOP

name: Starter Air Valve
rem: One may be inoperative CLOSED provided: a) Alternate starting procedures are used, b) Associated valve is manually closed after engine start, and c) Associated engine Air Turbine Starter (ATS), for in flight relights, is considered inoperative.
oproc: For an inoperative Starter Air Valve, do the manual override start procedure as follows: WARNING: Unless alternative procedure are established and used (to protect maintenance crew from being located between two running engines), cross bleed to the Right Hand Engine (RHE) is prohibited. Use APU or Ground Cart as source of bleed. For an inoperative Starter Air Valve, on ground do as follows: 1. Monitor EGT for indication of a hot start (Max EGT during start = 1054°C/1929°F). 2. Monitor N2 for indication of a hung start. 3. Make sure indicated speed does not exceed 20%. 4 Make sure EGT is below 250°C/482°F. 5 Make sure the associated engine RUN switch is selected to OFF. 6. In coordination with a ground coordinator instruct maintenance to manually drive the Starter Air Valve (SAV) open to initiate normal engine start. 7. Once N2 reaches 17%, set the Engine RUN switch to ON. NOTE: The fuel system is turned on by FADEC. 8. Verify on EICAS that N1, N2, EGT, oil pressure and fuel flow indications follow a normal start procedure. 9. If a hot or hung start is indicated, immediately select the associated engine RUN switch to OFF. 10. Following a hot or hung start, the affected engine to be cold soaked prior any subsequent engine re−starts attempts. 11. In coordination with the ground coordinator, at 50−55% N2, instruct maintenance crew to manually close the SAV. 12. For a subsequent In Flight Shutdown (IFSD) of the affected engine, perform windmill relight procedures in accordance with Non-Normal Procedures. CONTINUED NEXT PAGE
